The Police Inspector of Banashankari Police Station, Bengaluru has filed Police Report against the above named accused No.1 to 6 alleging that they have committed the offences punishable under Section 498A R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. It is the case of the Prosecution that the marriage of the informant was solemnized with the accused No.1 on 17-04- 2008 in presence of elders and family members by paying huge dowry.
The life of the informant was peaceful only for some days.
Later, all the accused started abusing the informant in a filthy language for one or the other reasons.
The accused were demanding further dowry.
All the accused were assaulting the informant by using filthy language.
These accused were demanding further dowry and pushed the informant out of their house.
The father of the informant has paid further huge dowry and sent back her daughter.
These accused has continued their cruelty on the informant.
These accused again assaulted the informant for dowry and pushed out of their house.
The informant has been blessed with three daughters.
But, these accused were abusing the informant that she had given birth to the daughters only.
The informant left with no option had been to the police station and lodged the information against these accused.
3. Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.117/2012 at Banashankari Police Station, Bengaluru City.
The accused No.1 to 6 were arrested and released on bail.
On completion of investigation, the Police Inspector of Banashankari Police Station, Bengaluru City filed Police Report against accused No.1 to 6.
After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to them.
As per the order sheet dated 21.03.2023, accused No.5 was reported as dead.
Hence, the case against accused No.5 was Abated.
The copies of the Police Report and other Prosecution papers are furnished to accused No.1 to 4 and 6 under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that accused No.1 to 4 and 6 have committed offences triable by this Court, charges have been framed and read over to them in Kannada language.
They have pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against accused No.1 to 4 and 6, the Prosecution has produced the oral evidences of PW1 and PW2 and documentary evidences as per Ex.P1 and Ex.P2.
There was a compromise Memo between the informant and the accused as per Ex.D1.

They have submitted that they have no defense evidence.

5. Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned Counsel for accused No.1 to 4 and 6. Perused the materials available on record.

9. To prove the guilt of the accused, the Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1 Shama Begum, who is a victim and informant and also CW3/PW2 Pyari Jan who is the mother of the informant have deposed that these accused tortured the informant for one or the other reasons.
They have taken huge dowry at the time of marriage and even after marriage.
These accused have not tolerated that the informant had given birth to three daughters.
These accused assaulted the informant and pushed the informant out of their house.
The informant left with no option had lodged the information against these accused.
These accused have not paid any maintenance to the informant till this date.
The informant is living with her parent.

10. Later, this informant has compromised with the accused and as per the compromise these accused have paid an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- to the informant as full and final settlement to the informant and her children.
Based on these compromise the informant has in her cross-examination has confirmed of the payment of Rs.5,00,000/- and withdrawn all the allegations made against these accused.

When the accused and the informant have compromised the dispute for the offences punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, this Court has found that there is nothing to convict the accused persons for the said offences alleged by the informant and held that the Prosecution failed to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts.

When the victim and the informant has compromised with the accused persons, there is nothing further to proceed against these accused and accordingly all the rest of the Prosecution witnesses are dropped Shamabegham vs Shaik Jabeeulla on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54467262/
3 by this Court as the matter is pending since 2012.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

11. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused No.1 to 4 and 6 for the offences punishable under Section 498A R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the accused No.1 to 4 and 6 are not found guilty for the aforesaid offences charged against them.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDERS Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, accused No.1 to 4 and 6 are hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Section 498A R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

Their bail bonds and surety bonds executed will be in force till completion of appeal period and thereafter, it will be stand canceled.
